Synopsis:
    Female Kurdish fighters (YPJ), formerly a key component of the U.S.-backed SDF in the fight against ISIS, are negotiating their future role within Syria's new post-Assad government. The SDF has been formally dissolved; the new Islamist-led administration has rejected YPJ integration into the army. Talks are now ongoing with the interior ministry for a special operations role. Broader Kurdish mistrust of the new rulers persists, underpinned by past violence against minorities and the new president's prior Al-Qaeda ties. The outcome carries significant social and political weight for Kurdish women in Syria.
